newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan credit demand rose 15 pct vs Dec - report.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan credit demand rose 15 pct vs Dec - report.

text.p: Brazilian consumer credit demand rose 15 percent in January compared with December, according to a study by daily newspaper Estado de Sao Paulo.
The increase surprised banks and financial institutions, which traditionally see a drop in demand for financing during the southern summer holiday period.
Consumer credit demand was up 40 percent compared with January 1996, Estado added.
"This is a very good result considering it is a holiday month with traditionally weaker sales," said Marcio Cipriano, vice-president of credit at Bradesco.
The number of defaults fell in December to its lowest level since the implementation of Brazil's currency stabilisation program in 1994, Estado said.

The number of loans which were more than 180 days overdue fell to 5.43 percent from 6.25 percent in November. Delays in payments of up to 30 days fell to 26.15 percent in December from 27.46 percent the previous month.
